body:
**Area:** area:config, **Phase:** phase:5-dx

**Why:** If an operator sets `NEXUS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT=1s` (valid but dangerous), the boot warning fires in the env path (`main.go:382`) but not in the `LoadYAML()` path. Operators loading from YAML never see the warning. Additionally, `ShutdownTimeout` is excluded from `ReloadHotReloadable()` — the only shutdown-related knob checked at SIGHUP is the warning at boot which is already there.

**What:** Add `ShutdownTimeout` to `ReloadHotReloadable()` so SIGHUP can re-evaluate it (even if it just logs the same warning at runtime rather than boot). Alternatively, move the warning into a shared `ValidateShutdownTimeout()` helper called from both `Load()` and `LoadYAML()`. Add `NEXUS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` to `.env.example` hot-reloadable list.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `ShutdownTimeout` is included in SIGHUP hot-reloadable checks
- `ValidateShutdownTimeout` (or equivalent) is called from both `Load()` and `LoadYAML()` paths
- `.env.example` includes `NEXUS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` in the hot-reloadable list
title: [enhancement] ShutdownTimeout warning only fires in env-path, not YAML-path

body:
**Area:** area:ratelimit, **Phase:** phase:5-production

**Why:** `ClientIPResolver` is constructed once at boot and has no `SetTrustedProxies([*]net.IPNet)` method. When `NEXUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` changes (the CIDR allowlist for `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Real-IP` honouring), the rate limiter keeps using the stale resolver. This creates a silent security gap: operators may believe they've tightened trusted proxies via SIGHUP but the rate limiter still uses the old (potentially spoofable) IP resolution.

**What:** Add `SetTrustedProxies([*]net.IPNet)` to `ClientIPResolver`. Wire it in the SIGHUP handler when `NEXUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` is in `NeedsRestart`. Also add `NEXUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` to the hot-reloadable list in `.env.example` (even though it requires restart, it should be in the list for visibility).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `ClientIPResolver` has `SetTrustedProxies([*]net.IPNet)` method
- SIGHUP re-evaluates trusted proxies and updates the resolver
- `NEXUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES` appears in `.env.example` hot-reloadable list
title: [enhancement] NEXUS_TRUSTED_PROXIES changes require restart but rate limiter uses stale resolver

body:
**Area:** area:ratelimit, **Phase:** phase:5-production

**Why:** The standard HTTP rate limiter (`RateLimitRPM`, `RateLimitBurst`) has `SetRPM`/`SetBurst` methods called on every SIGHUP (`main.go:1477–1479`), making it dynamically adjustable. The auth brute-force limiter (`AuthRateLimitRPM`, `AuthRateLimitBurst`, `AuthRateLimitWindow`) has **no such update mechanism** — `AuthLimiter` only has `SetOnBlock`/`SetOnReap`, no `SetRPM/SetBurst`. Operators under attack cannot raise the auth rate limit without a restart.

**What:** Add `SetRPM(int)`, `SetBurst(int)`, `SetWindow(time.Duration)` to `AuthLimiter`, then wire them in the SIGHUP handler alongside the existing `rateLimiter.SetRPM/SetBurst` calls. Add `NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_RPM`, `NEXUS_AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_BURST` to `ReloadHotReloadable()` in `config.go`. Update `.env.example` hot-reloadable list.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `AuthLimiter` has `SetRPM`, `SetBurst`, `SetWindow` methods
- SIGHUP handler updates auth rate limit parameters dynamically
- `.env.example` hot-reloadable list is updated
title: [enhancement] Auth brute-force rate limit is NOT hot-reloadable

**Area:** area:rag, **Phase:** phase:5-dx

**Why:** In `Store.IndexDir` batch path (rag.go:861-889), when `EmbedBatch` succeeds but individual `Upsert` calls fail (rare, but possible with SQLite write errors), the loop logs "rag indexed" per file but silently skips files whose `Upsert` returned error. There is no warning log for failed upserts after a successful embed, so operators cannot diagnose why fewer files were persisted than were embedded.

**What:** When a `PersistentStore.Upsert` fails after a successful embed, log a warning with the filename and error so operators can see that a file was embedded but not saved. This makes the partial-failure case observable rather than silent.

**Acceptance criteria:**

body:
**Area:** area:rag, **Phase:** phase:2-observability

**Why:** `EmbedCache.CacheStats()` (rag.go:403) acquires `c.mu` but the docstring on line 402 explicitly states "not thread-safe with concurrent access". `Store.Stats()` (rag.go:703) calls `s.CacheStats()` under the read lock at line 707, but this is called from the `/status` HTTP handler in `main.go` (line 1207) at the same time that concurrent `Retrieve` calls are hitting the cache from many goroutines. The `RWMutex` read-lock does not protect the atomic counters inside `CacheStats()` from being updated while `Stats()` reads them.

**What:** `EmbedCache.CacheStats()` should use atomic load for `c.hits` and `c.misses` instead of acquiring the mutex, since those counters are already `int64` and accessed atomically everywhere else. The fix is a one-line change per field — replace `c.mu.Lock/Unlock` in `CacheStats()` with direct atomic loads of `c.hits` and `c.misses`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `EmbedCache.CacheStats()` is safe to call concurrently with `Embed`/`EmbedBatch`/`Retrieve`
- `go test -race ./internal/rag` passes with no data race detected on `CacheStats()`
- `Store.Stats()` can be called from the `/status` handler concurrently with live traffic

labels.name: phase:2-observability
labels.description: PRD Phase 2: structured logging, metrics, savings dashboard

title: [bug] Store.CacheStats() is racy

body:
**Area:** area:rag, **Phase:** phase:5-production

**Why:** When `EmbedBatch` fails partway through a batch in `Store.IndexDir`, successfully embedded entries have already been appended to `s.examples` but `upsertExample` was never called (which would invalidate the HNSW index). The in-memory store now has N entries but the HNSW index still reflects the pre-batch state. Subsequent `Retrieve` calls use the stale index, potentially returning incorrect results. This silently corrupts search results with no error signal.

**What:** In `Store.IndexDir` batch path (line 861-889), when `EmbedBatch` returns an error, the loop continues to the next batch but `s.examples` already contains the successfully embedded entries from the failed batch — yet `s.index` is never set to `nil`. The non-batch path calls `s.upsertExample` per file which invalidates the index. The batch path never invalidates it. `PersistentStore.IndexDir` has the same problem: partial `Upsert` calls update the DB but the store's `upsertExample` is only called via the batch loop, not individually.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A batch embedding error during `IndexDir` does not produce stale HNSW search results
- `Retrieve` returns correct results immediately after a partial batch failure (fallback to brute-force is acceptable)
- A warning is logged when a batch fails with partial progress, so operators notice
title: [bug] Store.IndexDir batch errors leave HNSW index inconsistent

body:
**Area:** area:upstream, **Phase:** phase:2-observability

**Why:** When `Panel` serves from the arbiter cache, it returns `outcome.ArbiterCacheHit=true` and `outcome.ArbiterSkipped=true` but leaves `outcome.Similarity` at 0.0 and `outcome.SkipReason` empty. The handler records `ArbiterCacheHit` to a Prometheus counter, but the `skipped` bucket in `nexus_fusion_arbiter_total` grows identically for agreement-based skips and cache hits — operators cannot distinguish them. Computing `SimilarityRatio` for cache hits costs nothing (the content is already in memory) and would close this observability gap.

**What:** In `upstream.go`, after a cache hit is confirmed in `Panel` (around line 629), compute `outcome.Similarity = SimilarityRatio(r1.Content, r2.Content)` and `outcome.SkipReason = "cache_hit"` before the early return, matching what `PanelStreaming` does for agreement skips.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `Panel` on a cache hit sets `outcome.Similarity` to the Jaccard ratio of the two panel members
- `Panel` on a cache hit sets `outcome.SkipReason` to `"cache_hit"`
- No goroutine blocking or additional allocations on the hot path
- Existing tests in `upstream_test.go` pass

body:
**Area:** area:middleware, **Phase:** phase:5-production

**Why:** In `config.go:1465`, when `NEXUS_INJECTION_SCAN_ROLES` contains unrecognized values, a slog.Warn is emitted listing the unrecognized tokens. However, the warning fires even when the user correctly specified `"system"` (the default) alongside some valid-but-unnecessary values. The warning doesn't indicate which specific token caused it.

**What:** Refine the warning in `config.go` to only fire when the resulting roles differ from what the user likely intended:
1. Only warn when `unrecognized` is non-empty AND the resulting `roles` set is `{"system"}` (the fallback), because that means the user's entire input was discarded.
2. Include the offending token(s) and the resulting fallback in the warning message.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- A config with `NEXUS_INJECTION_SCAN_ROLES=system,user` does NOT log a warning (both are valid)
- `parseInjectionScanRoles` test coverage includes the case of partial-valid input
title: [P3] NEXUS_INJECTION_SCAN_ROLES warning is noisy and doesn't identify the offending token

body:
**Area:** area:router, **Phase:** phase:5-intelligence

**Why:** `containsWord` (dsl.go:169) builds and calls `regexp.MatchString` with a freshly constructed pattern on every invocation. `Categorize` calls it ~60 times per prompt (once per keyword across all `categoryKeywords` groups). On the routing hot path this means ~60 regex compilations + cache lookups per request. The docstring calls it "pure, cheap function" — but it's not cheap.

**What:** Replace the dynamic regex-per-call approach with pre-compiled `*regexp.Regexp` values. Each `categoryKeywords` entry in `confidence.go` should carry its own compiled `*regexp.Regexp` set at package init, and `DSL` should receive pre-compiled pattern slices rather than calling `containsWord` which re-compiles each time.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `BenchmarkCategorize` shows measurable improvement (aim for >3x faster) vs. current implementation
- All existing `containsWord` and `Categorize` tests continue to pass with no behavior change
- No allocation on the hot path for the common case (all-lowercase prompt, no regex compilation)

body:
**Area:** area:router, **Phase:** phase:5-dx

**Why:** The DSL checks pattern groups in a fixed precedence order: `fusionPatterns` → `formattingPatterns` → `localPatterns` → `unicodePatterns`. When a prompt matches multiple groups (e.g., "format this architectural diagram" matches both fusion and formatting), the first match wins silently. Operators tuning `NEXUS_DSL_*_PATTERNS` have no way to know that precedence is meaningful — and the current precedence (fusion > formatting > local) may not match their intent.

**What:** Document the precedence order explicitly in `.env.example` alongside each DSL pattern env var. Also add a sorted-by-precedence comment to `planner.go` where the groups are assigned.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `.env.example` documents the precedence explicitly for each DSL env var
- The `DSL` function's precedence order is unchanged (no behavior change, only docs)
- A comment block in `planner.go` explains the precedence at the point where patterns are checked
title: [ENHANCEMENT] DSL pattern precedence is undocumented — overlapping keywords produce confusing results
